question: Can chapter 3's three reused sets (the lamp, the landing, the gap) be made snowy from their own paint and run 014's painted snow, for free, so each spread reads as a new place without moving anything?
why: Chapter 3 (docs/plans/2026-11-15-finish-chapters.md) reuses all three of its sets, 'all snowy'. Playtests: each spread must feel like a new place. Build plan: docs/plans/2026-11-16-finish-chapter-3.md, run 020.
sameAcrossJobs: Free pass first: make_snow.py (numpy, Pillow) keeps every piece's alpha exactly (run 007's lit window), caps upward-facing edges and recolours sand from art/room-fx/weather/snow-cover.png (run 014), rimes the lamp's glass. Paid only for a piece the free pass fails: one 2K seedream5_pro repaint from that piece's own image (downscaled under 5 MB as Figure 1), standing pieces on magenta cut with run 006's recipe, then only its snow kept inside the original's alpha, so nothing can move.
decideBy: Each snowy spread in the emulator beside its unsnowy self: it reads as the same painted page under snow, not a filter (the look bar).
Nothing moved: marks, hinges and anchors equal the base sets' (client/src/show/chapter-3.test.ts), and crossings land where they did.
Telemetry fps per spread at least 72; the owner judges in the headset.
learnEvenIfRejected: Whether a set can be given a season for free from its own paint, which would make any later chapter's weather on the page cheap.
reusableOutput: art/sets/the-lamp-snow/, the-landing-snow/, the-gap-snow/ (snowy pieces and set.json each), and make_snow.py for any later season.
estimateNote: 0 for the free pass. 27 if the three grounds need a repaint (the likeliest to read as a filter); each candidate moves from candidateJobs into jobs only after its free version has failed, and is reconciled against its known price (9) in lane B's per-job cost ledger, or one job per invocation until that ledger lands.

The cliff faces and the dark water of the chasm keep their paint exactly, with no snow on the water. The bare paper edges stay exactly as in Figure 1. Hand-painted traditional watercolor with a fine graphite pencil outline, from a vintage natural history picture book. Soft pigment washes, visible paper grain, gentle edges. No characters, no footprints, no text, no border, not a photo of a book.
